sections.html:
Pickens County sits in the north Georgia mountains with Jasper as its seat. It had an estimated 37,167 residents by mid-2025, and 26.8 percent of them are 65 or older. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $332,700, and 81.2 percent of housing is lived in by the owner. Median gross rent is $1,136, and builders took out 277 permits in 2025.

With so many older owners, many already hold local exemptions. A buyer who loses those exemptions at closing may see a different bill than the seller paid, and a seller who understands that can explain it before the contract is signed.

sections.h2: Who bills and who values property?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner bills, collects and distributes, and also processes motor vehicle registration. The Board of Tax Assessors appraises property, approves exemptions and reviews appeals. Grand jurors appoint the Board of Equalization that hears the administrative appeal.

Pickens County tax offices
Office or serviceContact
Tax Commissioner address1266 E. Church Street, Jasper, GA 30143
Tax Commissioner phone(706) 253-8882
Tax Assessor phone(706) 253-8700
Commissioner office hoursMonday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

A drop box in front of the Administration Building is open around the clock. Cards cost a 2.60 percent convenience fee at the counter, on the web or by phone, and an e-check adds a flat $3.00. Partial payments are welcome, though interest keeps running on whatever stays unpaid. Owners can ask online for a mailing address change, and the site keeps forms, an excess funds page and a tax sale page for bidder registration.

November 15 is the date for real estate and business personal property. Manufactured homes get a January bill and an April 1 deadline. A US Postal Service postmark counts as timely, but a metered postmark does not.

  • Interest runs at the prime rate plus 3 percent, divided across 12 months.
  • A 5 percent penalty comes at day 120, recurs every 120 days and stops at 20 percent.
  • Taxes more than 90 days late can lead to a recorded FIFA lien at the courthouse.
  • The office can levy on the property but calls that a last resort.

Mail goes to the homeowner only, never the lender, so an owner with an escrow account has to pass the bill along. If you sell near the due date, ask whether the lender already paid.

Day 45 after the notice date is the last day. The Board of Tax Assessors looks again at its value first and responds with a decision. If the board holds firm, the Board of Equalization takes the appeal up at a hearing. Superior Court is the final stop.

  • You can appeal on taxability, value, uniformity compared with similar property, or the denial of an exemption.
  • You can request arbitration at the time of filing instead of going to the Board of Equalization.
  • Returns are filed at the assessors' office in the first three months of the year. A return that declares your own value can preserve appeal rights if the board later changes the number.
  • Taxable value begins at 40 percent of market value. County commissioners and the school board each pick a millage rate.

Ask the assessors for the exact mailing date on your notice, since the 45 days count from that date and not from the day it reaches you.

The standard homestead subtracts $2,000 from assessed value before the county, school and State operating rates are applied. The Board of Tax Assessors accepts applications, and the books close April 1. Anything received later counts toward the following year. New owners should carry in a copy of their warranty deed.

  • A Pickens-only exemption erases the school levy for owners aged 62 or older with a gross household income of $25,000 or under.
  • A standard elderly school exemption of up to $10,000 for owners 62 or older whose net income does not exceed $10,000.
  • A general elderly exemption of up to $4,000 for owners 65 or older under the same income limit.
  • A disabled veteran exemption of up to $50,000 of assessed value.
  • A deferral that postpones the bill without erasing it, open to owners 62 or older with household income at or below $15,000.

A floating exemption is open to owners 62 or older whose income is $30,000 or lower. It stands in for other state and county exemptions, and the first bill may rise. Ask the assessors before applying for it.

Dial (706) 253-8882 to learn what the parcel owes, and ask whether earlier years, interest or a lien are involved. The commissioner's site has a tax sale page with procedures and a bidder registration form, which shows how the office handles properties that stay delinquent.

The sale contract, applied by the closing attorney, sets the split of the year's tax. If the seller held an elderly or local school exemption, the buyer starts without it and must apply for a homestead on the new home. Deed copies are kept by the Clerk of Superior Court.

Mobile homes on the lot are billed in January with an April 1 due date and need a current decal, which is issued when the tax is paid. Ask the commissioner whether a mobile home carries a separate bill before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What a buyer needs from the tax office
sections.html:
A buyer who relocates from another state will deal with the same Jasper office that bills the house, since the commissioner also registers vehicles. A buyer should expect to bring the following to tag a car:

  • For a car with no loan: the out-of-state title, the registration from the previous state, proof of Georgia insurance, a Georgia driver's license showing a Pickens County address, and the current mileage.
  • For a car with a loan: the loan agreement with the lender's full name and address, the T-17 affidavit of the lienholder, and the same insurance, license and mileage items.

The license requirement means a buyer should update the address on the license after closing. The commissioner's site also has a search for property and mobile home taxes, so a buyer can check the parcel's bill history before signing.

An unpaid bill after November 15 grows by interest each month, picks up a 5 percent penalty at 120 days, and may be recorded as a FIFA lien after 90 days. Credit bureaus can read that filing, and a buyer's title search will find it. Pay before the lien is recorded if you can.

If a lien is already filed, the closing attorney pays the tax, interest, penalty and fees from your proceeds and obtains the release. A cash sale skips the lender's wait and review, which can help when time is short, but the balance still comes out of what you receive at closing.

faqs.q: What is the Pickens County property tax due date?
faqs.a: November 15 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: How can I pay a Pickens County tax bill?
faqs.a: Walk-in payments take check, cash or card. Online payment takes cards and e-checks. A drop box outside the Administration Building stays open day and night. Cards add a 2.60 percent fee and e-checks add $3.00.

faqs.q: How many days do I have to appeal in Pickens County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, starting on the date of the assessment notice. Step one is the Board of Tax Assessors. Step two is the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.

faqs.q: Does a Pickens County homeowner need to reapply for homestead after buying?
faqs.a: Yes. A new owner or new residence must apply again, and the assessors need it by April 1 for it to count that year.

faqs.q: Does late Pickens County property tax hurt my credit?
faqs.a: It can. Lien filings at the courthouse are public, and credit bureaus may pick them up.
